qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Canadian retail deposit franchise oligopolist with #2 market share in personal deposits and lending, complemented by an extensive US retail banking branch network. Canadian franchise maintains an unassailable low-cost funding moat and pricing power. Primary erosion risks: severe growth constraints from the US regulatory asset cap (imposed by the OCC/Fed following AML guilty plea), multi-billion-dollar compliance remediation costs, executive turnover, and fintech competition.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). While TD Bank operates an entrenched Canadian retail banking franchise with #2 domestic market share and proven pricing power, as a fractional-reserve commercial deposit-taking bank it structurally fails the Munger Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency standard. Operating at ~15x asset/equity leverage and funded by demand deposits, its solvency inherently relies on depositor confidence and central bank/CDIC backstops ('kindness of strangers'). Compounded by the growth-restricting US regulatory asset cap and compliance remediation costs following its 2024 AML settlement, it cannot qualify as a fortress compounder.
qualitative.evidence: Canada's second-largest bank by assets with a premier Canadian retail deposit franchise and large US branch network. Historically generated 13-16% ROE (5-year median GAAP ROIC 32.8%). However, commercial fractional-reserve banks structurally fail Gate 6: balance sheet carries over C$1.9T in total assets supported by C$127.8B in common equity (~15x leverage) and C$225.3B in long-term debt liabilities. Operating cash flows swing wildly (-C$69.6B in FY2025 and -C$65.3B in FY2023) due to wholesale funding and deposit dynamics. In addition, the US operations face an unprecedented growth-limiting asset cap (US$434B cap imposed by OCC/Fed) and multi-year compliance remediation following the October 2024 US$3.09B criminal AML settlement.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
